q: Which of the following is an input device?
explain: A scanner sends a digital image of a paper original into the computer. Plotter, speaker and printer all deliver output.

q: Which device provides touch input and visual output in the same unit?
explain: Touch sensing on a touchscreen is input while its display is output, so it combines both.

q: The QWERTY keyboard layout gets its name from:
options: The first six letters of the upper alphabetic row
The first six letters of the alphabet
explain: QWERTY simply reads the first six letters of the top letter row, left to right.

q: Which layout, used in France and some French-speaking regions, swaps A/Q and Z/W compared with QWERTY?
explain: AZERTY exchanges the positions of A with Q and Z with W; some other keys also differ.

q: Which statement about the Backspace and Delete keys is correct?
options: Backspace removes the character after the cursor; Delete removes the one before it
Both keys always remove the entire line
Backspace usually removes the character before the cursor; Delete removes the one after it
Backspace deletes files permanently; Delete only edits text
explain: Backspace works backwards from the cursor, Delete works forwards (or removes the selected content or item).

q: Which group contains only modifier keys?
explain: Ctrl, Alt and Shift change the action of another key pressed with them.

q: A traditional full-size PC keyboard commonly has how many keys?
explain: Traditional full-size PC keyboards commonly have 101 or 104 keys, although counts vary by model and regional layout.

q: Which statement about keyboard technology is correct?
options: A keyboard optically scans each page typed on it
A keyboard does not optically scan documents; many scan an internal key matrix to detect keypresses
Every keyboard uses a laser to detect keypresses
A keyboard must be connected by a USB cable to work
explain: Keyboards do not scan paper. The scanning that happens is of an internal grid (matrix) of key switches. Wireless keyboards also exist.

q: Who invented the computer mouse in the early 1960s at Stanford Research Institute?
explain: Douglas Engelbart invented the mouse at SRI. Gerpheide is linked to touchpad technology, Benjamin to roller-ball pointing and Kirsch to scanning.

q: A mouse sensitivity setting is usually expressed in:
explain: DPI is the popular unit for mouse sensitivity; CPI (Counts Per Inch) is technically more precise for sensor reporting.

q: The capacitive technology behind the Cirque GlidePoint touchpad was developed in the late 1980s by:
explain: Gerpheide developed the capacitive technology; the touchpad should not be credited simply to Apple.

q: Which pointing device stays stationary while the user rolls an exposed ball with the thumb or fingers?
explain: A trackball has a fixed base; only the ball rotates, so no sliding movement across a desk is needed.

q: Which scanner type pulls loose sheets through the device and suits batches of documents?
explain: Sheet-fed scanners move the paper past the sensor. A flatbed keeps the original still on glass.

q: In 1957, a rotating-drum scanner to feed images into a computer was built by a team led by:
options: Russell Kirsch at the US National Bureau of Standards
Douglas Engelbart at Stanford Research Institute
explain: Kirsch and colleagues at the National Bureau of Standards built this early scanner, so scanner invention should not be credited simply to Xerox.

q: After scanning a printed page of text, the result is first stored as:
options: Editable text in a word processor
An image that OCR can later convert into text
explain: A scanner only produces an image. OCR software must then recognise the characters.

q: A standard retail barcode usually identifies:
options: The price only, with no database needed
The product, with the price fetched from a database by the POS system
explain: The POS system looks up price and description in a database using the identifier. Only some specialised formats can encode price directly.

q: QR code was introduced in 1994 by a team led by Masahiro Hara at:
options: Toyota Motors as a subsidiary brand
explain: The developer was a DENSO division that became DENSO WAVE; calling it simply a Toyota subsidiary is imprecise.

q: Which statement about scanning a payment QR code in a UPI app is correct?
options: Scanning alone always completes the payment
QR codes cannot carry payment information
Only a barcode reader can read a UPI QR code
Scanning shows details for review; the payment still needs the user to authorise it
explain: The app displays the payment details and the user must review and authorise them; scanning alone does not authorise payment.

q: Which technology is used to check shaded bubbles on examination answer sheets?
explain: Optical Mark Recognition detects which response positions are marked on a properly designed form.

q: Which statement about OCR is correct?
options: It works only when the paper is placed on a flatbed glass
It can process an existing image without a new physical scan
It decides which bubble is shaded
explain: OCR works on scans, photos of text or image-based PDF pages that already exist.

q: The Indian nine-digit MICR sort code is arranged as:
options: 3 digits bank + 3 digits city + 3 digits branch
3 digits branch + 3 digits bank + 3 digits city
3 digits city + 3 digits bank + 3 digits branch
explain: The format CCC BBB RRR gives city first, then bank, then branch.

q: Which item is NOT contained within the nine-digit MICR sort code?
explain: The cheque serial number is a separate field of the MICR line, not part of the nine-digit city-bank-branch code.

q: MICR characters on a cheque are printed with:
options: Fluorescent ink across the top of the cheque
Invisible ink read only by lasers
Ordinary ink read by a mark sensor
Magnetic ink, in a band near the bottom of the cheque
explain: MICR uses magnetic ink and a magnetic reader, and the data sits in a designated band near the bottom.

q: A microphone is best described as which type of device?
options: An output transducer that converts electricity into sound
An input transducer that converts sound pressure into an electrical signal
A storage device for audio files
A purely digital converter with no analogue stage
explain: Microphones turn sound into electrical signals; speakers and headphones do the reverse.

q: Which set lists the main parts of a moving-coil (dynamic) microphone?
options: Diaphragm, voice coil and permanent magnet
explain: Sound vibrates the diaphragm and coil in a magnetic field, producing a signal by electromagnetic induction. Diaphragm plus backplate describes a condenser microphone.

q: On a traditional PC sound card, which colour is the microphone input?
explain: Pink is the microphone input, lime green is the main stereo output, light blue is line-in and black is rear-speaker output on some systems.

q: A hydrophone is used to detect:
explain: A hydrophone converts underwater sound to electrical signals, for example in ocean research.

q: Which statement about mic input and line input is correct?
options: Mic input accepts a stronger signal than line input
Both accept exactly the same signal strength
Line input accepts a stronger signal than mic input, so a microphone may need a preamplifier first
Line input is used only for hydrophones
explain: Mic input expects a weak signal; line input expects stronger line-level signals from a player, mixer or preamplifier.

q: Which pixel size corresponds to 4K UHD video?
explain: HD (720p) is 1280 x 720, Full HD (1080p) is 1920 x 1080 and 4K UHD is 3840 x 2160.

q: Which statement about megapixels (MP) is correct?
options: One megapixel is about one million pixels, but more MP alone does not guarantee a better photo
One megapixel is exactly one thousand pixels
More megapixels always give a better photo
Megapixels measure the storage space of a memory card
explain: Lens, sensor, light and processing also decide image quality.

q: A resistive touchscreen detects input through:
options: Pressure bringing conductive layers into contact
explain: Resistive screens respond to pressure. Capacitive screens detect a change in capacitance.

q: A traditional light pen works only with which type of display?
explain: Traditional light pens use screen light and display timing, which a CRT provides. They do not work on ordinary modern LCD screens.

q: Which stylus technology imitates finger touch and usually has no battery?
explain: A passive capacitive stylus simply mimics a finger. Active pens carry electronics and a battery.

q: Which statement about a graphics tablet is correct?
options: It always includes a built-in screen
It captures the complete paper image like a scanner
It works only with CRT displays
A pen tablet may have no display, so the user watches a separate monitor
explain: A pen display combines the screen with the drawing surface; a plain pen tablet does not.

q: Which statement is correct about a joystick?
options: It is a stick pivoting on a base for directional control, and a gamepad is not a standalone joystick
It is a handheld controller with no moving stick
It is a pen-shaped input tool for touchscreens
It is used only to scan fingerprints
explain: A joystick uses a pivoting stick. A gamepad has buttons and thumbsticks but is a different controller.

q: An iris scanner captures the pattern of:
options: The coloured ring around the pupil
explain: The iris is the coloured ring; the pupil is the central opening. Near-infrared light is commonly used.

q: PIR in a motion sensor stands for:
explain: A PIR sensor detects changes in incoming infrared radiation; it does not directly measure body temperature.

q: Which statement correctly separates speech recognition from speaker recognition?
options: Speech recognition finds what is said; speaker recognition finds who is speaking
Speech recognition finds who is speaking; speaker recognition finds what is said
Both only convert text into sound
Both work only on written text
explain: STT turns spoken words into text, while speaker recognition identifies a voice owner.

q: A contactless smart card communicates with its reader using:
explain: Contact cards touch the reader contacts by insertion; contactless cards use short-range RF.
